disease_label_per_paper: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia presenting with hypercalcemia, multiple osteolytic lesions, and acute renal failure
presentation_summary: 14-year-old girl presented with 3 months of generalized body aches that began in the lower back and progressed to both legs and chest.
Exam showed generalized small lymphadenopathy, localized chest and leg tenderness, and palpable stiff tender liver and spleen.
Initial CBC showed hemoglobin 8.5 g/dL, WBC 9.4 x10^9/L, platelets 137 x10^9/L, and peripheral smear without abnormal cells or blasts.

Chemistry and imaging showed hypercalcemia, elevated urea/creatinine, calcium 13 mg/dL, phosphate 2.3 mg/dL, uric acid 7.6 mg/dL, albumin 2.7 g/dL, multifocal osteolytic lesions, collapsed T12 vertebral body, mild L4 wedging, bilateral mild hydronephrosis, renal parenchymal disease, and scant ascites.
Bone marrow and flow cytometry confirmed pre-B-cell ALL.
